subject: Observability pricing: slab flex & advanced UI bundle clarification
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@pioneerhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Observability packaging question for upcoming pilot

Hi Jonas / Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — really helpful. A couple procurement and architecture folks asked for a short follow-up on how you price the observability add-ons (retention for traces/OTel, advanced dashboards) because Pioneer Health is a regulated workload and we need clarity on commitments vs pay-as-you-go.

High-level context:
- Estimated baseline: ~1.2B tokens / month (generation + logging)
- Traces: 3M spans/day, need 90-day retention for auditable traces
- Want a 3-month pilot, then evaluate 12-month commit options

Specific asks:
1) Explain slab (committed storage/retention) vs metered pricing for tracing — which you recommend for predictable budgets and auditability?
2) Advanced dashboards — is this a standalone annual add-on or included under retention tiers? Any seat/visualization limits?
3) Sample SOW or procurement doc we can pass to legal/procurement (format: PDF/DocuSign preferred).

Can you share a short matrix with scenarios (pilot, 12mo slab, metered with smoothing) and an estimate of discounts at commit levels? Procurement would also like to see any overage smoothing / grace periods.

Attachments: usage_sample.csv (we attached a small sample of expected monthly traffic).

Best,
Alex
Alex Torres
Head of ProdOps — Pioneer Health

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-19T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability packaging question for upcoming pilot

Alex — thanks for the clear note and the sample. Looping in Naomi on billing specifics; below is a compact matrix and recommended path. I attached an editable pricing matrix (pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a draft SOW template we usually use for pilots.

Quick recommendation (short):
- Pilot (3mo): offer credits that cover ~75% of expected trace storage and dashboard seats so Pioneer can validate queries and dashboards under real load. No slab commit required for pilot.
- Production (12mo commit): slab for trace retention (storage commitment) + seat-based license for advanced dashboards. Slab gives predictable monthly charge and preserves auditability (we reserve dedicated retention tier and priority retrieval).
- Metered fallback: if Pioneer prefers variable costs, we can do metered tracing with a smoothing band (monthly spend averaged over quarter) and an automatic cap to prevent bill shock.

Pricing examples (very high level):
- 12mo slab (recommended): 18% discount vs list for retention + 10% off dashboard seats for a 12mo commit at expected volumes. Includes SLA for retrieval latency and compliance audit logs.
- Metered + smoothing: no upfront discount; include 30% pilot credit and 2-month grace window on overages with capped per-month overage multiplier (x1.2) during first quarter.

Next steps:
1) Confirm pilot start date window (we can start provisioning within 10 business days of signed SOW).
2) I’ll share an updated SOW and a tailored pricing tab — Marcus will review discount bands.

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-20T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Discount guardrails and pilot concession for Pioneer Health

Internal note — copying pricing playbook guidance so we’re consistent. Proposed concession for this deal (DEAL-9127):
- Pilot: 30% credits against retention/dashboards for 3 months (covers access and up to 80% of expected trace storage).
- Commercial: 12-month slab at 18% off retention list + 10% off dashboard seats for commitments >= $120k/mo equivalent.
- Overage smoothing: allow a 2-month overage buffer for first quarter; overage multiplier capped at x1.15 for months beyond buffer.

Risks: Pioneer is a regulated customer — we should tighten retrieval SLA (we can offer 24-hour guaranteed archival retrieval in the slab). Also ensure KMS integration, which could add a small one-time onboarding fee.

Action items for Jonas: please include the two concession lines in the SOW draft; ask legal for a short Appendix A for KMS/onboarding.

Marcus Lin
Head of Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference

If you can add the export/exit language and a ramping schedule into Appendix A and circulate the DocuSign link, procurement is ready to review. We’ll aim to sign the pilot by end of next week pending those changes.
